Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 13:11:00 +0000
Subject: Initial request — TIA scope and subprocessor evidence

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of Helios's security gating for vendor onboarding in the EU, legal and privacy have asked us to confirm a few things before we can move to PO: specifically TIA/DTIA scoping, UK IDTA applicability, and a detailed subprocessor map with evidence of controls (encryption at rest, access controls, and certs).

Can you: 
- Confirm whether Redwood treats our EU traffic as routed/processed inside EU-only regions and whether there are fallback routes to US regions?
- Send a consolidated subprocessor list (including cloud infra, logging, observability, and any managed services) and attestations/cert links where available.
- Confirm whether the UK Addendum / IDTA will be required for Helios (we have some UK processing in scope).

We have filled out a short questionnaire — attaching draft answers so you can validate: helios_tia_questionnaire_filled.xlsx (attached).

Timing: Helios procurement is aiming to complete vendor due diligence by EOD Friday (2027-02-19). Any chance you can get a first-pass response and evidence by Wednesday?

Appreciate it,
Daniel
Head of IT & Privacy
Helios Therapeutics

[attachment: helios_tia_questionnaire_filled.xlsx (xlsx)]

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the questionnaire. We can certainly get you a consolidated response. Quick answers up front:
- Primary processing for EU customers is performed in EU regions (Amsterdam and Frankfurt) unless a customer requests otherwise; there are documented failover paths to US regions for disaster recovery. We can provide the routing policy and regional SLOs.
- I'll share an up-to-date subprocessor export and a short attestation pack with SOC/Security links.
- On the UK IDTA: because you have UK processing, the UK Addendum will be relevant; our legal team can confirm the exact placement in the DPA.

Plan: I'll loop in Kimberly (legal) and Laura (security ops) to assemble evidence. We expect to send a first-pass packet by Wednesday 17:00 UTC. If Helios needs anything earlier, tell us which items are highest priority.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_202702.pdf. Quick notes inline:

Dylan / Kimberly / Laura —

Thanks for the fast turn. The subprocessor export looks useful. A couple of clarifications from legal: 
- For LogStream and EdgeHoldings we need signed attestations on letterhead confirming no access to plaintext customer data and the logging retention policy.
- For routing: can you confirm if customer can elect to block US failover entirely? If not, we need the contractual controls (e.g., encryption in transit, and the fallback triggers).

If you can provide those two items and the draft UK Addendum note, we can keep procurement on track. We'll need the signed attestation PDFs by Friday EOD.

Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached are the items requested:
- redwood_tia_response_20270215.docx — answers to the questionnaire with cross-references to controls and routing behavior.
- redwood_subprocessors_202702.pdf — updated with two signed attestations from LogStream Inc. and EdgeHoldings (on letterhead) included as scanned pages.

For dedicated/private customers we support strict EU-only processing by configuration and tooling.
